captured_with: LibJciHitachi 1.7.2 + fork fix/tolerate-undecodable-device-responses; awsiotsdk 1.31.0; official app 雲端智慧控 11.30.600 (iOS) used only to read prompts

messages.status-secondary/response: status_response.schema.json (same key set; topic is requested by the official app, not by the library)
messages.statistic/response: NOT CAPTURED as JSON (only the 6-byte frame was seen on this topic, from a running unit)

observed: always exactly these 6 bytes, from three different units, 2026-09-03 .. 2026-09-17
per device: in the same poll other units on the account answer JSON

correlates with the unit running: a unit switched on from Home Assistant answered the frame on the next poll; a unit switched off went back to JSON within 6 minutes; in the 00:02 capture the only unit with status Switch 1 was the only one answering the frame; at 16:57 all three answered the frame (power state not recorded)

BUT running is not sufficient: at 01:13 on 2026-09-17 the unit that had answered the frame since 23:52 answered JSON again while its status said Mode cool, Switch 1 (Home Assistant showed it cooling at 25 °C); what changed on the unit at that moment is not known
not correlated with the official app's freeze-clean prompt (shown for units that answered JSON)
shadow info still answers JSON for the same unit; status/response was JSON for the running unit in the same poll where its registration/response was the frame

nested_mqtt_publish_answer.seen: once, 2026-09-17 00:36:12, on registration/response from an idle unit (Switch 0) that had answered the frame-free JSON on the previous polls
observed: 761 bytes: exactly the length of that unit's normal registration/response JSON (registration_response_gw-B.json is 761 bytes)

bytes 0..706 are a complete MQTT PUBLISH packet: type 0x32 (PUBLISH, QoS 1), remaining length 704, topic <identity>/<identity>_<gw>/status/response (134 bytes), packet id 4709, then a 620-byte status/response JSON (26 keys, Switch 0, CleanNotification 1)
bytes 707..760 are the first 54 bytes of a second MQTT PUBLISH (0x32, remaining length 714, topic length 144) cut off mid-topic
one poll earlier (00:35:22) the same unit's status/response event fired without JSON data; two polls later (00:38:29) it answered normally again
nested_mqtt_publish_answer.meaning: unknown; the content is a raw MQTT byte stream delivered as a payload. Placeholders in the fixture keep the original lengths so the framing stays valid.

not_observed_in_this_profile.note: max_temp / min_temp are derived by the library from TemperatureSetting in registration/response, not cloud fields
